title: Downstate review – razor-sharp tragicomedy set in a home for sex offenders
text:
Booth theatre, New York City 

 Liza Colón-Zayas and Thomas Sadoski star in a provocative drama that brings nuance – and dark humor – to the stories of four child sex offenders

 Fred doesn’t get out much these days, thanks to the incident that put him in a wheelchair. But the elderly man finds joy in small things: the music of Chopin, fruity smoothies prepared by his doting housemate Dee, as well as Nutter Butter cookies. Not everyone sees Fred as harmless. Minutes after we meet him, a man a few decades his junior tells him that he is a fundamentally evil person and describes in cold, chilling detail exactly how he would carry out his murder.

 Fred is one of four registered sex offenders whose life in a group home is the subject of Downstate, a razor-sharp black comedy by playwright Bruce Norris. As well as Fred (Frances Guinan), the house residents include buff gym rat Gio (Al’Jaleel McGhee), taciturn Felix (Adrian Martinez) and the thespy, Diana Ross-obsessed Dee (K Todd Freeman), a surrogate caretaker for the old man. The men have been somewhat thrown together as an unlikely family, and the yellowing wallpaper and mismatched furniture has certainly seen better days. But the spot is a comfortable enough place for the men to land, although the baseball bat propped up by the front door shows that they are ready for violence if it comes their way.
